newsitem.title: USA: June confidence reading highest since moonwalk.
newsitem.headline: June confidence reading highest since moonwalk.

text.p: Consumer confidence rose in June to the highest level since the summer of 1969, when an American walked on the moon, a business research group said on Tuesday.

The Conference Board said its consumer confidence index rose to 129.6 in June from a revised 127.9 in May. The latest reading was the highest since 131.7 in August 1969, the month after astronauts Neil Armstrong and Edwin "Buzz" Aldrin became the first people to walk on the moon.
The report comes as the economy is into its seventh straight year of growth with low inflation and unemployment that has fallen to 4.8 percent, the lowest in 23 years.
"Overall, the economy is doing quite well and there seems to be no signs of a let up in growth," said Lynn Franco, associate director of The Conference Board's Consumer Research Centre.

The report could raise eyebrows at the Federal Reserve when policy-makers meet next week to weigh their next move on interest rates. The central bank raised short-term rates in March, the first increase in more than two years, in a bid to slow the economy and ward off inflation.

Many analysts have said the Fed was likely to hold rates steady at the July 1-2 meeting, as they did last month, based on other recent reports indicating the economy was slowing after growing at a strong 5.8 percent rate in the first quarter.

The Conference Board report comes after separate readings on confidence by the University of Michigan have risen to record highs. Confidence readings are watched closely because consumer purchasing fuels two-thirds of the economy.

Still, despite high confidence levels and plentiful jobs, consumers do not appear to be spending more money on cars, homes and major appliances. Consumers' plans to buy those types of goods within the next six months fell in June from May, the Conference Board survey said.
About 36 percent of consumers said business conditions were good, up from 33 percent in May. A like percentage said jobs were plentiful, up from about 35 percent in May, it said.
The board also said the expectations component of the index fell to 110.7 in June from a revised 111.4 in May.

Paul Kasriel, chief economist at Northern Trust Co. in Chicago, said that if consumer confidence continues rising, a rebound in consumer spending may be nearing. "It suggests that one of these days consumers are going to start buying again," he said.
The board's May reading was revised to 127.9 from 127.1.
